title: Digest shared types, version 2
description:
Shared serialization types for the digest contract v2. Nothing here resolves over the network: the $id values are stable identifiers, not endpoints.

Two rules shape this file and are worth stating once. First, presentation is not stored: a check carries an `id` and the UI resolves its question, section order and prose from the shipped check catalogue, exactly as it resolves an issue's label, meaning and chart from CLIENT_ISSUE_TYPES. Storing the wording would mean two copies of it that can disagree, and v1 proved they do. Second, every count that could be read as a rate names its denominator in the same object, because a numerator alone invites a reader to invent one.

instant.title: An absolute instant, UTC
instant.description: RFC 3339 with a `Z` offset. Server time, never client-reported wall clock: a browser with a skewed clock would otherwise move a call to the wrong day.

interval.title: A closed time interval
interval.description: Both ends inclusive and both absolute. An interval is what makes a finding navigable — it is what the sample browser and the charts are scrolled to.

reportingDay.title: The UTC day a call is assigned to
reportingDay.description: `YYYY-MM-DD`, from the UTC date of the call's START. A call that begins at 23:50Z and ends at 00:20Z belongs entirely to the day it started; it is not split. One rule, applied in storage, aggregation and on screen.

unit.title: The unit of an observed value
unit.description: Closed on purpose. A value whose unit is not in this list cannot be formatted by the UI, and an unformatted number on a quality page is worse than an absent one. `none` is for a dimensionless count that is not a quantity, such as a state label's ordinal.

observedValue.title: One measured figure behind an outcome
observedValue.description: What the rule actually read. `value` may be null: a check can fail on the ABSENCE of a figure (no remote report, a counter that reset) and the UI must show that absence rather than a zero. `threshold` is present only when the rule compares against one, so a reader can see the margin rather than take the verdict on trust.

subjectKind.description: Mirrors IssueScope in src/schema/ClientIssueTypes.ts, so a finding's subject and the issue that evidences it describe the same thing.

subject.title: What a per-client check was evaluated against
subject.description: A client-scoped check has no `id`. A track- or connection-scoped one carries the id the existing client page already keys its sections on, which is how an evidence link lands on the right row rather than the right page.

issueRef.title: A built-in issue that evidences an outcome
issueRef.description:
`type` is a key of CLIENT_ISSUE_TYPES. Deliberately only the type, the instant and the payload: the label, category, severity, meaning, implication, remedy, chart and highlight fields all live in that registry and are resolved at render time.

Only the 37 built-in types may appear. Observer-generated detector findings, application events and enriched metadata are out of scope for this contract, and a producer that emits one here has broken the scope boundary rather than extended the schema.

eventRef.title: A built-in client event that evidences an outcome
eventRef.description: `type` is a value of ClientEventTypes. Used mostly by continuity and coverage checks, where the evidence is a state change rather than a statistic.

evidenceTarget.description: Which existing section of the client or call page an evidence link opens. The first four mirror IssueTimelineTarget; `samples` is the raw sample browser and `client` is the client page itself.

evidenceRef.title: Where the UI should navigate to inspect this
evidenceRef.description: The contract's answer to "show me". It names an existing section and, where one applies, the id to select, the chart to open (an IssueChartKind) and the interval to scroll to. It never describes a new view: a digest that asks for a chart the dashboard does not have is a digest the dashboard cannot honour, so the chart vocabulary is the one already shipped.

gapReason.description: Why a stretch of a client's time could not be assessed. `stats-collection-gap` and `tab-hidden` come from built-in events; `before-first-sample` and `after-last-sample` are the edges of what was observed at all.

coverage.title: How much of the time could be assessed at all
coverage.description:
Read before any count anywhere in the document. `assessedSeconds + unassessedSeconds` equals `observedSeconds`; time outside the observation window is not counted as either, because a client that joined late was not unassessable, it was absent.

This object is the reason a quiet period and a broken pipeline cannot look alike.

outcome.title: The answer to a check
outcome.description:
`passed` — the rule ran against sufficient evidence and found no fault.
`failed` — the rule ran and found the fault.
`not-assessable` — the evidence the rule needs is absent, partial or reset. NEVER rendered as a pass, and never counted as healthy.
`not-applicable` — the subject cannot have this fault: no inbound video, no audio track, no outbound media.

The distinction that matters most: a check resting only on "no issue fired", with no corroborating statistic, is `not-assessable`. An absent detector is not a healthy call.

outcomeCounts.title: How a roll-up answered, with its denominator
outcomeCounts.description: `evaluated` is the denominator and equals the sum of the four. It is stored rather than left to the reader because a reader that adds the four to get it will be wrong the day a fifth outcome exists.

clientSessionRef.title: One client session, addressable
clientSessionRef.description: The full triple. `clientId` is unique within a call and not globally, so a client session IS `callId` + `clientId` — and `roomId` is here because the dashboard's URL is /{roomId}/{callId}/{clientId}. Without it a drilldown list would have to open every call digest just to build a link.

callRef.title: One call, addressable
callRef.description: `roomId` for the same reason as above: /{roomId}/{callId} is the route.

provenance.title: Which code produced this, and when
provenance.description: `rulesVersion` is the one to read when two digests disagree about the same call. Bumping it means the same inputs may now answer differently; existing digests are NOT regenerated, they keep the answer their rules gave, and the UI says which rules produced what it is showing.
